QF.id: VI Functions of DP Account Operations_13

question.text: On death of a joint holder in a demat account, the surviving holders can:

answer.text: Either open a new account and transmit the balance, or — if requested within 365 days — delete the deceased holder's name from the existing account
Only close the account and distribute the securities
Continue using the account without any changes
Only transmit to a new account — deletion from existing account is not possible

explanation.text: The Logic: Two routes are available: (1) transmit the holdings to a new account opened by the surviving holders (old account closed), or (2) delete the deceased holder's name from the existing account when requested within one year (365 days) of the date of death, supported by a death certificate attested by a Notary/Gazetted Officer. The Trap: 'Continue without changes' would leave a deceased person's name on an active financial account, which is not permitted. Note: If the deletion request is made after 365 days, the surviving holders must use the transmission process and open a new account rather than deleting the name from the existing one.
